The Maid In The Meadow

From the playing of Coláiste Árainn Mhóir, on the album Rabharta Ceoil. Transposed down from Bbmaj.

Simplified setting from their playing, since they play a lot of variations.

The A Part fairly closely resembles the “regular” Maid In The Meadow, and the B Part is a bit further removed (a few groupings of three notes were removed from the “regular” version, and some different phrases). See:
https://thesession.org/tunes/942

The B Part resembles the B Part of The Maid At The Well:
https://thesession.org/tunes/752

Re: The Maid In The Meadow

Re: The Maid In The Meadow
Someone has listed this as composed by “Walker Jackson”. What’s the evidence for that ?

↳ Posted by Kenny 2 years ago.

It is one of the few tunes which can be definitely proven to be one of his. It appears in ‘Jackson’s Celebrated Irish tunes, 1774’ a pamphlet by Jackson, under it’s original title of Cossey’s Jig (also in the session under yet another title of Cassey’s Jig. The website it is best found in is: https://pipers.ie/source/gallery/?galleryId=51&pageIndex=0 it is the 1st tune on the 1st page. The Maid In the Meadow title is 20th Century according to the annotation in Trad Tune Archive, being from 1920. Curiously the website doesn’t show the full tune, missing the last line of each tune at 1st. You have to click on the tune to get the full pdf.

↳ Posted by Graham Shaw on March 17th, 2024.

The Maid In The Meadow, X:12

Seamus Ennis version in The Wandering Minstrel recording, named “The stone in the Field”

Played after Gillian’s Apple and The Wall of Liscaroll.

This is a three parts version, the same version in three parts which Seamus Ennis also plays in Feidlim Tonn Ri’s castle with the same name Stone in the Field.

↳ Posted by UPipes & harp on May 9th, 2024.

The Maid In The Meadow, X:13

customized from version 12, where the last 4 bars of the C part are the same as the last four bars of the B part.

I also added a return down to D at the end of Part A for transition to Part B.

Seamus Ennis did thus a lot, returning down to D and adding grace notes below the note played.

↳ Posted by UPipes & harp on May 13th, 2024.

Re: The Maid In The Meadow - three part version played in 1974 on the pipes by Séamus Ennis

https://www.itma.ie/playlists/padraics-picks-november-2024/?track=1

This is some fine traditional playing, but the sound quality is pretty bad. In particular, watch out for the nasty squeak right at the beginning. You were warned. Still, very well worth a listen or three IMO.

“Séamus Ennis holding court at the 1974 pipers Tionol in Co. Louth.”
ITMA catalogue: https://itma.accesstomemory.org/tda-258348-1-277861
The given title in the ITMA catalogue for this jig/recording is The stone in the field.

It’s fairly close to the X:12 and X:13 scores shared by UPipes & harp above - but it’s not entirely the same setting, as far as I can see from a quick look and listen.
